title: Who Gets Built First?
explanation:
Construction goes from the inside out: base classes first, then members (in declaration order), then the constructor body. By the time `Derived()`'s body runs, everything it might use already exists.

Destruction is the exact reverse: `~Derived()`'s body runs while its members and base are still alive, then the members are destroyed, then the base.

This guaranteed reverse order is what makes RAII work: a lock or file opened later is always released before the things it depends on.
